stories.headline: Microsoft launches MAI-Thinking-1 reasoning model, trained from scratch with zero distillation

key_facts.fact: MAI-Thinking-1 is a 35B-active / 1T-total parameter MoE reasoning model with a 256K-token context window, unveiled at Microsoft Build 2026 on June 2.
key_facts.excerpt: Today we are introducing MAI-Thinking-1, Microsoft AI's reasoning model. It is a medium-sized model that stands among the strongest models in its weight class... 35B active, ~1T total parameters, MoE... 256k token window.

key_facts.fact: The model scored 52.8% on SWE-Bench Pro, 97.0% on AIME 2025 and 87.7% on LiveCodeBench v6 according to Microsoft's technical report.
key_facts.excerpt: MAI-Thinking-1, a 35B active / 1T total parameter MoE that stands among the strongest models of similar size on STEM reasoning and coding tasks (e.g., 52.8% on SWE-Bench Pro, 97.0% on AIME 2025, and 87.7% on LiveCodeBench v6).

key_facts.fact: Microsoft trained the model on 30 trillion tokens on 8K GB200 GPUs without distillation from third-party models, excluding AI-generated content from pre-training.
key_facts.excerpt: pre trained from scratch on 8K GB200 GPUs on a Microsoft-operated cluster within the Azure platform... we ran a main pre-training phase of 30 trillion tokens... free of any distillation data.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft says independent human raters on Surge prefer MAI-Thinking-1 to Claude Sonnet 4.6 in blind side-by-side evaluations, and the model matches Claude Opus 4.6 on SWE-Bench Pro.
key_facts.excerpt: Independent human raters on Surge prefer MAI-Thinking-1 for overall quality in blind side-by-sides to Sonnet 4.6 across single and multi-turn tasks... competitive with Claude Opus 4.6 on SWE-Bench Pro.

key_facts.fact: MAI-Thinking-1 is part of a family of seven new in-house models released at Build, including MAI-Image-2.5 and MAI-Code-1-Flash.
key_facts.excerpt: the Microsoft AI Superintelligence Team released a family of seven new in-house models, starting with MAI-Thinking-1– Microsoft AI's first reasoning model. Trained from scratch with zero distillation on enterprise grade, clean and commercially licensed data.

key_facts.fact: MAI-Image-2.5 debuted at #2 in the Image Edit Arena with a score of 1401, advancing the Pareto frontier per LMArena.
key_facts.excerpt: MAI-Image-2.5 has officially released from @MicrosoftAI landing at #2 in the Image Edit Arena (Single-Image-Edit) with a score of 1401 and advances the Pareto frontier!

stories.headline: DeepSeek to raise $7.4B in maiden funding from Tencent and CATL at $52-59B valuation

key_facts.fact: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek is set to raise about 50 billion yuan ($7.4 billion) in its first funding round from investors including Tencent and CATL.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek is set to raise about 50 billion yuan ($7.4 billion) in its first funding round from investors including Tencent Holdings and CATL, people with knowledge of the matter said.

key_facts.fact: Post-money valuation is expected between 350 billion and 400 billion yuan, or roughly $52 billion to $59 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The fundraising could value the company after the investment at between 350 billion yuan and 400 billion yuan, or between $52 billion and $59 billion, the people said.

key_facts.fact: Founder Liang Wenfeng is committing 20 billion yuan of personal capital; Tencent is considering 10 billion yuan and CATL 5 billion yuan as the largest external investors.
key_facts.excerpt: Founder Liang Wenfeng has committed 20 billion yuan of his own money to the round... Tencent is considering an investment of 10 billion yuan, while CATL is looking at putting in 5 billion yuan.

key_facts.fact: Fewer than 10 investors are expected to participate, with the round set to close within the next couple of weeks; additional names in talks include IDG Capital, Monolith Capital, NetEase, JD.com and China's national AI fund.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek is also in advanced talks with China's national artificial intelligence fund, gaming developer NetEase, and e-commerce giant JD.com for potential investments... Other potential investors include Hong Kong-based IDG Capital and Monolith Capital.

stories.headline: ChatGPT hits 1B monthly active users in record time; Claude grows 640% YoY to 56M

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT crossed 1 billion global monthly active app users in May, roughly three years after launch, making it the fastest app ever to the milestone per Sensor Tower.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI's ChatGPT has crossed 1 billion global monthly active app users, becoming the fastest app ever to reach the milestone... ChatGPT reached 1 billion MAUs in May, roughly three years after launch, surpassing the pace set by apps including Google Maps, TikTok, Instagram and YouTube.

key_facts.fact: Sensor Tower estimates Claude had 56 million global monthly active app users in Q2-to-date with year-over-year growth of about 640%, versus ChatGPT's 62% YoY growth.
key_facts.excerpt: As of the second quarter to date, Claude had 56 million global monthly active app users, while its year-over-year MAU growth of about 640 per cent significantly outpaced ChatGPT's 62 per cent growth.

key_facts.fact: U.S. ChatGPT users who installed Claude in Q1 2026 spent 5% less time on ChatGPT one month after installation compared with their average usage in the prior eight months.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. ChatGPT users who installed Anthropic's Claude app in the first quarter of 2026 spent 5 per cent less time on ChatGPT one month after installation, compared with their average usage in the prior eight months.

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT's share of worldwide downloads among six major AI apps tracked by Sensor Tower fell to 47% in Q2 2026-to-date, down from 67% a year earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: Among six major AI apps tracked by the firm, ChatGPT accounted for 47% of worldwide downloads in the second quarter of 2026 to date, down from 67% during the same period a year earlier.

key_facts.fact: Sensor Tower noted it took between five and eight years for Google Maps, Chrome, YouTube, Messenger and TikTok to reach 1 billion global monthly active users.
key_facts.excerpt: Sensor Tower said it took between five and eight years for Google's Maps, Chrome, YouTube, Meta's Messenger and TikTok apps to reach 1 billion global monthly active users.

stories.headline: AI music startup Suno raises $400M at $5.4B valuation, led by Bond Capital

key_facts.fact: Suno raised $400 million at a $5.4 billion valuation, with Bond Capital leading the round alongside IVP, Forerunner and Union Square Ventures; existing backers Lightspeed and Menlo Ventures also participated.
key_facts.excerpt: Suno Inc., a startup that enables people to make music using artificial intelligence, has raised $400 million at a valuation of $5.4 billion. Bond Capital, which has invested in OpenAI and Kalshi, is leading the round alongside venture capital firms such as IVP, Forerunner and Union Square Ventures.

key_facts.fact: The valuation more than doubled from the $2.45 billion mark set in Suno's November 2025 Series C, which raised $250 million.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's valuation has doubled since its $250 million funding round seven months ago. The latest investment makes Suno the highest-valued company among AI music startups.

key_facts.fact: Suno passed 2 million paid subscribers in February 2026 and is tracking toward $300 million in annual revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: Suno passed 2 million subscribers in February and is tracking toward $300 million in annual revenue.

key_facts.fact: The startup employs about 200 people and plans to grow headcount by up to 70% before year-end, per co-founder and CEO Mikey Shulman.
key_facts.excerpt: The company currently employs about 200 people and aims to grow its workforce by up to 70% before the end of the year.

stories.headline: Trump signs scaled-back AI executive order focused on cybersecurity and voluntary review

key_facts.fact: President Trump signed an executive order on June 2, 2026 establishing a voluntary framework for evaluating advanced AI models with significant cybersecurity capabilities, rejecting mandatory licensing or preclearance.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. President Donald Trump signed Tuesday an executive order establishing a voluntary framework for evaluating advanced artificial intelligence models with significant cybersecurity capabilities in a directive that rejects mandatory licensing or preclearance requirements.

key_facts.fact: The order shortens the federal pre-deployment review window for covered frontier models from 90 days in earlier drafts to up to 30 days.
key_facts.excerpt: AI companies would voluntarily provide the federal government access to frontier models before release, but now it will be for 'up to' 30 days instead of the 90-day timeline included in previous drafts.

key_facts.fact: The order directs Treasury, NSA and CISA to develop classified benchmarks to assess advanced cyber capabilities of AI systems and identify 'covered frontier models'.
key_facts.excerpt: A key component of the order directs the Department of the Treasury, National Security Agency and Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to develop and maintain a classified benchmarking process for assessing the advanced cyber capabilities of AI systems.

key_facts.fact: It also establishes an AI cybersecurity clearinghouse coordinating vulnerability scanning and patching with industry and critical infrastructure operators in voluntary collaboration.
key_facts.excerpt: the Secretary of the Treasury... shall form an AI cybersecurity clearinghouse, in voluntary collaboration with the AI industry and operators of critical infrastructure, that coordinates and deconflicts scanning for software vulnerabilities, discovers and validates such vulnerabilities, and coordinates and prioritizes remediation and distribution of vulnerability patches.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman publicly backed the order, saying it 'gets the balance right' between developing the best models and getting cyber tools into defenders' hands.
key_facts.excerpt: @sama: the US should lead on AI by continuing to develop the very best models, making sure they're safe, and getting cyber tools into the hands of trusted defenders. the new EO gets the balance right.

stories.headline: Alibaba releases Qwen3.7-Plus multimodal agent model with 1M-token context

key_facts.fact: Alibaba released Qwen3.7-Plus, a closed-source multimodal model that unifies vision and language into an agent foundation, with a 1 million token context window.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba's Qwen3.7-Plus supports text, video and imagery inputs at low cost of $0.4-$1.6 per 1M token but it's proprietary... like its immediate predecessor Qwen3.7-Plus is available only under a 'closed' commercial license via proprietary application.

key_facts.fact: Pricing is set at $0.4 to $1.6 per 1M tokens depending on input modality, undercutting prior Qwen tiers, and the model is positioned as a multimodal agent that can operate GUI and CLI interfaces.
key_facts.excerpt: Multimodal interactive hybrid agent: unified GUI & CLI operation across vision and language.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba says Qwen3.7-Plus delivers text-benchmark performance that approaches the company's top-tier Max models.
key_facts.excerpt: Performance1: Text Benchmarks Qwen3.7-Plus delivers competitive text performance that approaches Max-tier models across the board.

stories.headline: Microsoft unveils Project Solara, an Android-based platform for agent-first devices

key_facts.fact: Microsoft introduced Project Solara at Build 2026, an Android-based operating system platform for devices built around AI agents rather than traditional apps.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft unveils Project Solara, an Android-based platform for agent-first devices, with concept hardware and pilots planned at Best Buy, Target, and others.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft demonstrated two concept devices: an always-on desk device powered by a MediaTek SoC, and a wearable badge-style device.
key_facts.excerpt: The first device for Project Solara is a desk device concept, powered by a MediaTek SoC that can basically be an ambient always-on, always-available device that can handle your agents for you... Microsoft showed off two devices at Build: a desk concept and a badge concept.

key_facts.fact: The platform is built around three principles: enterprise readiness, just-in-time UI that adapts to form factor, and extensibility so customers can bring their own agent.
key_facts.excerpt: Project Solara is about 3 things: * Being enterprise ready * JIT UI that adapts to the form factor * Extstensible so you can bring your own agent.

key_facts.fact: Pilots with Best Buy, Target and other retailers are planned, framing Solara as Microsoft's bet on a new hardware category in the agent era.
